name: boiler_param_identification
title: Classical fuel-oil boiler: parameter identification from the nominal point
summary: Companion of the classical ON/OFF fuel-oil boiler reference model: the three boiler parameters (gas-water conductance AU_gw, envelope conductance AU_wenv, fuel mass flow M_dot_f) are identified from nominal-point data (efficiency, useful power, water flow, supply temperature) and one stand-by heat-loss measurement; combustion products via the mean specific heat procedure cpbar, both exchangers epsilon-NTU.

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of TM-0493 (66 numeric values, EES X7.888): compare_solution.py reports 66 common variables, 2 differ (rtol=0.001): t_g_ex 1.84e-3, AU_gw 1.36e-3; at rtol=1e-2 all agree. The deviations trace to the ideal-gas mean c_p of cpbar (0.06-0.08 % between EES 7.888 and CoolProp).
verification.reference: EES stored solution of BOILER_PARAM_IDENTIFICATION_EES_MODEL_SBJL080212.EES (66 numeric values, EES X7.888)
verification.notes: Identification chain recomputed by hand: M_dot_f = Q_dot_u_n_ON/(eta_N*LHV) = 1.29200e-3 kg/s; epsilon_wenv = Q_dot_wenv_n_OFF/(C_dot_w*(t_w_su-t_env)) = 0.0073012, AU_wenv = -C_dot_w*ln(1-epsilon_wenv) = 18.324 W/K - both match the EES stored values exactly. cpbar mean c_p differs 0.075 % (c_p_p) / 0.06% (c_p_g) between backends and propagates to t_adiab (1929.06 vs 1930.49 C), t_g_ex and AU_gw. 'only in CoolSolve: 2' are the subscript names V_dot_w_l\h and V_dot_w_l\h_n (absent from the extracted EES variable records; M_dot_w confirms V_dot = 2150 l/h).
